text:
Both teams arrive stung. Buffalo lost 3-2 in overtime at Chicago two days ago, a game that ended the Blackhawks' six-game winless run, and the Sabres are winless in three (0-2-1) without Konsta Helenius, Justin Danforth and Matt Grzelcyk. Dallas lost 8-3 at home to Winnipeg, a game the Jets won after trailing by two, and the Stars are missing Miro Heiskanen, with Tyler Myers now up to 20:30 a night from 17:10. Buffalo also lost 4-0 here on Oct 8, a game Dallas deserved to win 45% of the time, meaning the Stars took that share of simulated replays of every shot.

The chance numbers are close. Each team has about 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, and our model has Dallas ahead only slightly, 3.17 to 2.78. The special-teams matchup to watch is the Stars' power play, worth 0.79 expected goals a game, against a Buffalo penalty kill allowing 0.77, and the Sabres take 4.1 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen sits 3.4 goals saved above expected below par this season after a +9.1 year in 2025-26. Jake Oettinger is at +5.0 this season but has slipped to .842 over his last five.

Tage Thompson is our top Sabre at 37% to score, and Wyatt Johnston and Jason Robertson lead Dallas at 37% each. Our under-the-radar pick is Tyler Seguin, a third-liner with 2.9 expected goals in his last 10 games and a 21% chance to score tonight. Jamie Benn is one point from 1,000.
